title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Using a sanitary tee to join two horizontal drain lines is a critical mistake in DWV (Drain, Waste, Vent) systems. Sanitary tees are designed for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections. When installed horizontally, the sharp sweep fails to properly direct solid waste down the flow path, leading to frequent clogs and splashing. Instead, horizontal-to-horizontal junctions require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn. Proper fitting selection ensures smooth flow velocity, prevents solid buildup, and keeps drainage systems compliant with standard plumbing codes.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines

Using a sanitary tee to join two horizontal drain lines is a critical mistake in DWV (Drain, Waste, Vent) systems. Sanitary tees are designed for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections. When installed horizontally, the sharp sweep fails to properly direct solid waste down the flow path, leading to frequent clogs and splashing. Instead, horizontal-to-horizontal junctions require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn. Proper fitting selection ensures smooth flow velocity, prevents solid buildup, and keeps drainage systems compliant with standard plumbing codes.
